newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ARI queries Country Road results.
newsitem.headline: ARI queries Country Road results.

text.p: Advisers to Country Road Ltd's third largest shareholder, Australian Retail Investments Pty Ltd (ARI), have written to the fashion retailer raising concerns about its half year results and current strategies.

"ARI has serious concerns regarding the company's performance and future position in the market in light of the interim result," J.T. Campbell & Co wrote on ARI's behalf in a letter to Country Road chief executive Mike Howell.
In late February ARI, run by Peter Lew, the son of former Coles Myer Ltd chief executive Solomon Lew, bought about nine percent of Country Road but played down speculation of an imminent takeover.
Country Road's net profit for the six months to February slumped to A$1.09 million from A$5.53 million a year earlier.

In its seven-page lettler, J.T. Campbell & Co, a Melbourne-based merchant bank, asked Country Road to clarify items in the results including sales figures, cost allocation, working capital, inventories, receivables and management's shareholdings.

It also queried the company's decision to pay a two cent interim dividend in light of its lower earnings, higher capital employed, negative cashflow and Howell's tepid outlook for pre-abnormal second half results.
